documents.unit: Student Handbook, Academic Honor Code and Academic Dishonesty (Baseline Policy on Generative AI Use in Student Work)
documents.title: The Academic Honor Code and Academic Dishonesty (includes Baseline Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence Use in Student Work)
documents.summary: The Student Handbook honor code section includes a university baseline that treats any unauthorized AI use in graded work as cheating. Faculty may permit AI for specific assignments if stated in the syllabus, and permitted use must be cited. Sanctions for dishonesty start at course failure plus probation.
documents.stance_why: The baseline policy bans AI 'for any part of any academic exercise' 'unless explicitly permitted by the instructor' and treats silence as 'not permitted', so AI is banned unless explicitly permitted: restrict.

units.why: The baseline says all student work 'will be generated by students themselves', so students may not have AI produce submitted work; coded P19 (not P29) because the point is generation by AI, and it covers every stage from brainstorming to final.
units.anchor: will be generated by students themselves, working individually or in groups

units.why: A definition of generative AI with named examples ('Grammarly, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DALL·E, GitHub Copilot') sets what the policy covers, so it is a scope definition (P61) with informs modality.
units.anchor: any technologies that can autonomously produce text, images, code, media, translations

units.why: The policy carves basic spelling and grammar correction out of its definition of AI ('does not consider ... to be AI'), narrowing scope while letting faculty prohibit them; scope definition, P61.
units.anchor: does not consider basic spelling and grammar correction tools

units.why: 'Unless explicitly permitted by the instructor' AI use for any part of any graded exercise is academic dishonesty: a default ban on graded work. P01 chosen over P36 because the main content is the default ban; the cheating classification is secondary.
units.anchor: Unless explicitly permitted by the instructor, the use of AI tools for any part

units.why: Lists 'using AI to generate ideas, outlines, titles, or drafts' as dishonest absent permission, which forbids AI-produced work product at early stages; P19.
units.anchor: using AI to generate ideas, outlines, titles, or drafts

units.why: Forbids 'using AI to summarize course readings addressed in the assignment'. A study-aid use would fit P14, but here it is banned for the assignment; no type fits a ban on summarizing better than P19.
units.anchor: using AI to summarize course readings addressed in the assignment

units.why: 'submitting AI-generated text or media as one's own' is listed as dishonest; the core of P19.
units.anchor: submitting AI-generated text or media as one’s own

units.why: 'using AI to complete problem sets, coding tasks, or data analysis' names code and analysis explicitly; AI producing the solutions, P19.
units.anchor: using AI to complete problem sets, coding tasks, or data analysis

units.why: 'having AI edit or revise written work' is banned without authorization, which covers editing and checking of one's own work (P21 rather than P19 since the student wrote the text).
units.anchor: having AI edit or revise written work

units.why: Unauthorized assistance from 'an AI system' is 'treated as academic dishonesty', classifying misuse under the integrity process; P36.
units.anchor: including an AI system — to assist with their work, without authorization, is treated

units.why: Equating AI with 'purchasing work, hiring others' treats AI as an outside helper under existing rules for outsourcing; P45 (not P36, already coded for the preceding sentence) because the point is the analogy to human helpers.
units.anchor: outsourcing any part of the academic process to AI tools

units.why: 'Individual faculty members may choose to be more restrictive' lets instructors tighten the baseline, an instructor-set rule above a floor; P04.
units.anchor: Individual faculty members may choose to be more restrictive than above

units.why: Faculty 'may choose to permit the use of generative AI tools for specific assignments or purposes', so permission is set per assignment by the instructor; P04.
units.anchor: may choose to permit the use of generative AI tools for specific assignments or purposes

units.why: Permissions 'must be clearly stated in the course syllabus or on the assignment prompt', a requirement to state AI expectations; P09.
units.anchor: must be clearly stated in the course syllabus or on the assignment prompt

units.why: Permissions 'must define the extent and nature of permitted use' (brainstorming only, coding assistance, citation help): a condition on what the instructor states. P09 (communication content) rather than P05 because no named tiers are set.
units.anchor: must define the extent and nature of permitted use

units.why: Permissions 'may differ from one assignment to another within the same course', placing the decision at assignment level; P04.
units.anchor: may differ from one assignment to another within the same course

units.why: 'In the absence of a clear statement ... AI is not permitted' gives the fallback when a syllabus is silent; P06.
units.anchor: the default assumption is that AI is not permitted

units.why: 'Students should not assume that permission ... on one assignment implies blanket permission for the course' limits permissions to the assignment; P11.
units.anchor: Students should not assume that permission to use AI on one assignment implies blanket permission

units.why: When AI is allowed students 'must: Clearly cite and attribute the AI tool used', a disclosure duty naming the tool; P24, with the extra detail coded separately.
units.anchor: Clearly cite and attribute the AI tool used

units.why: Students must 'Describe the nature of its use' with an example, detail required in the citation (tool, how used); P25 as it specifies what the citation must contain.
units.anchor: Describe the nature of its use (e.g., “used ChatGPT to generate initial outline”)

units.why: Students must 'Follow any course-specific citation guidelines or use an accepted academic citation format (e.g., APA, MLA)': citation format rule; P24.
units.anchor: use an accepted academic citation format (e.g., APA, MLA)

units.why: 'Failure to properly attribute AI use — even when permitted — constitutes a breach of academic honesty' makes nondisclosure itself the violation; P28.
units.anchor: Failure to properly attribute AI use — even when permitted — constitutes a breach

units.why: Improperly cited or unpermitted AI use 'may ... constitute plagiarism, fabrication, or cheating' and 'When not permitted, it is cheating': classification as misconduct; P36.
units.anchor: When not permitted, it is cheating
units.policy: When AI use is permitted but improperly cited, it may, depending on the circumstances, constitute plagiarism, fabrication, or cheating.

units.why: Departments 'may further clarify this general definition in writing' and violations of such statements count as university violations: units may set their own clarifications and they bind; P04 (rule set at unit level).
units.anchor: Academic departments and programs, at their option, may further clarify this general definition

units.why: 'Faculty members should state, in advance, their policies and procedures concerning examinations and other academic exercises' and the next sentence points AI questions to the baseline policy; communication of expectations, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty members should state, in advance, their policies and procedures

units.why: Students 'should assume that any external assistance ... is prohibited unless specifically authorized' on exams; a general rule in the cheating section next to the AI cross-reference, so exam closed-assistance rule, P22 (not AI-specific wording).
units.anchor: should assume that any external assistance

units.why: The sanctions for dishonesty, which the policy declares AI misuse to be, are 'failure in the course and probation through tenure' or suspension: concrete penalties; P37.
units.anchor: failure in the course and probation through tenure
units.policy: For a first offense of academic dishonesty, the sanction is failure in the course and probation through tenure, or failure in the course and suspension for one or more semesters.

units.why: Second offenses draw 'failure in the course and suspension ... or expulsion': escalation by offense, P37.
units.anchor: failure in the course and suspension for one or more semesters or expulsion
units.policy: For a second offense of academic dishonesty, the sanction is failure in the course and suspension for one or more semesters or expulsion.

documents.unit: AI at Colgate (Office of the Provost and Dean of the Faculty, with CLTR and ITS)
documents.title: Teaching and AI
documents.summary: Faculty-facing provost page that leaves AI use to individual instructors and asks them to communicate expectations clearly. It points to ITS and CLTR resources and consultations, and gives data-privacy and procurement cautions.
documents.stance_why: The page says AI in teaching 'is a faculty member's individual choice' and asks faculty to be clear with students, setting no rule itself: delegates.

units.why: 'AI ... is a faculty member's individual choice' puts the decision with each instructor; P04.
units.anchor: is a faculty member's individual choice

units.why: Faculty 'are asked to be very clear with their students about any expectations' on use or prohibition of AI; P09.
units.anchor: Faculty are asked to be very clear with their students about any expectations

units.why: Defines generative AI ('uses machine learning models to create new content'), setting scope; P61.
units.anchor: a type of artificial intelligence that uses machine learning models to create new content

units.why: ITS 'holds a series of events inviting the campus community to explore various AI tools', helping faculty learn AI; P63.
units.anchor: ITS holds a series of events inviting the campus community to explore various AI tools

units.why: ITS 'has reviewed and compiled a list' of generative AI tools, a vetted list, with a caution that some are 'not allowed or ... discouraged in specific courses'; P50 (vetted tools) rather than P17 as no tool is provided.
units.anchor: ITS has reviewed and compiled a list of some of the most popular

units.why: 'Course-based consultations' offered by ITS 'for faculty members interested in course-based AI uses' support faculty learning; P63.
units.anchor: ITS offers consultations for faculty members interested in course-based AI uses

units.why: Says it is 'important to clearly communicate guidelines for appropriate use' and whether students may use generative AI; P09 for communicating expectations.
units.anchor: it is important to clearly communicate guidelines for appropriate use to your students

units.why: The CLTR 'sample syllabus statement' is offered to help instructors state a policy; P09 (support for the syllabus statement), no tiers offered.
units.anchor: The CLTR has created a sample syllabus statement to help you get started

units.why: Tells faculty to refer to the Honor Code and to be 'as clear as possible in their syllabi, and in speaking with their classes' about student AI use; P09.
units.anchor: Instructors should be as clear as possible in their syllabi

units.why: 'Avoid entering confidential data ... into AI tools' (finance, HR, medical, student records) protects data; P50.
units.anchor: Avoid entering confidential data, per the University’s Data Categorization Policy, into AI tools.

units.why: Warns that tools 'using default settings may not be private and could expose sensitive data', the reason for the data rule; P50.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools using default settings may not be private

units.why: Faculty and staff are told to 'consult with ITS before procuring' AI tools so ITS verifies privacy and security: review of AI tool acquisition; P65.
units.anchor: consult with ITS before procuring internal or external AI tools

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred. Sections of the honor code on plagiarism and cheating beyond the AI baseline were coded only where they bear on AI (sanctions, exam assistance, attribution).
